raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Accelerate native FlashInfer prefill on SM120 by converting referenced FP8 KV
pages once into bounded BF16 scratch. The earlier release implementation
improved input-token throughput by up to **10.1%** in recorded paired
cold-prefill tests, while retaining persistent FP8 storage and BF16 queries.

## Claims

- Disabled by default; BF16 queries and decode retain their existing precision.
- Most promising for large prefill chunks with repeated KV reads; the extra
  copy and memory cost can outweigh any benefit on other workloads.
- Separate scratch ownership per live metadata object, with native fallback
  for unsupported modes, small prefills, budget limits and allocation failure.

## Validation

Measured on the earlier release implementation with identical request bytes,
checkpoint and speculative-decoding settings in both arms:

| Cold-prefill case | Native input tok/s | Expanded input tok/s | Improvement |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Shorter | 8,823 | 8,936 | +1.3% |
| Intermediate | 6,145 | 6,525 | +6.2% |
| Longest | 3,478 | 3,828 | +10.1% |

These are input tokens divided by server-reported prefill time, with zero
prefix-cache hits and one measured pair per case. The longest case's prefill
latency fell **9.2%**. These measurements describe the prior implementation;
they are not current-main benchmarks or decode-throughput gains. Workload
and checkpoint details are withheld; the supplementary validation document
provides a public-model follow-up procedure.

Validation combines earlier GPU numerical/reference and end-to-end serving
checks with checks of this upstream port:

- The release-based implementation passed GPU and serving checks. Its host
  helper logic is preserved, and eight compiled SM120 kernel instruction
  sections match byte for byte using the same toolchain.
- On this checkout: 10 CPU metadata tests with upstream conftest, 50 Triton
  CPU-interpreter cases, CLI setting/bounds checks, eight offline SM120
  compilations, and all applicable pre-commit hooks passed. Kernel cases
  cover every finite E4M3 encoding and addresses beyond 2 GiB.

The supplementary [validation record](https://github.com/tireiron/vllm/blob/349c772899cbda8349ae6a096b7fccc5571019f4/VALIDATION.md)
contains reproduction commands; the [portable CPU check](https://github.com/tireiron/vllm/blob/349c772899cbda8349ae6a096b7fccc5571019f4/validate_kernel_cpu.py)
is available alongside it. CPU checks used released runtime
dependencies. This port's SM120 serving integration, performance and model
evaluation have not been rerun with current-main dependencies because a
dedicated test device is unavailable. Added GPU helper tests are selected
by existing attention CI; that CI does not exercise the SM120-only serving
path. No current-main speedup or model-accuracy result is asserted.

## Details

The native mixed-dtype prefill path converts FP8 cache tiles for successive
query tiles. Gathering referenced page entries once per layer and prefill
step lets BF16 attention reuse the converted values. The cast preserves finite
E4M3 values exactly, and attention still applies the original K/V scales.
Attention reductions may differ numerically.

The scratch cap is per live metadata object; overlapping objects allocate
independent buffers up to that capacity. This can reduce serving capacity.
Compare prefill/first-token latency with expansion disabled, including the
copy cost, and check mixed-load decode latency, throughput and memory. A
kernel speedup alone does not establish an end-to-end serving benefit.

Related work: [#55065](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55065) uses
FP8 queries and a different SM120 backend;
[#63328](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63328) handles sparse MLA/FA4
on datacenter Blackwell. This change targets dense/GQA native prefill with
BF16 queries. Earlier cache-conversion work also exists in
[FlashInfer #1304](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/1304);
the merged [FlashInfer #6445](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6445)
materializes NVFP4 pages to FP8 for a different TRTLLM prefill path.
The separate query-scaling fix
[#53754](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53754) is not included.
The existing TRTLLM dequantizer applies scales while converting and uses a
rectangular block table; this path preserves raw FP8 values and compact native
paged metadata instead. Maintainer feedback on placing this optimization in
vLLM versus FlashInfer would be useful.

AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, documentation and this draft.

@@ -0,0 +1,135 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Compare native FP8 prefill with gather/cast plus BF16 attention.
+
+Check whether avoiding repeated FP8 conversion offsets the extra page copy.
+Uses generated tensors and illustrative power-of-two sizes. Planning is
+outside the timed region; results measure a layer kernel path, not model
+serving throughput. Measure serving latency and capacity separately.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import statistics
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.v1.attention.ops.fp8_prefill_cache import expand_cache, plan_expansion
+
+
+def measure(call, repeats):
+    for _ in range(5):
+        call()
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    samples = []
+    for _ in range(repeats):
+        start, end = (
+            torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True),
+            torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True),
+        )
+        start.record()
+        call()
+        end.record()
+        end.synchronize()
+        samples.append(start.elapsed_time(end))
+    return {
+        "median_ms": statistics.median(samples),
+        "min_ms": min(samples),
+        "max_ms": max(samples),
+    }
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--query-tokens", type=int, default=4096)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--kv-tokens", type=int, nargs="+", default=[4096, 16384, 65536]
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--layout", choices=["HND", "NHD"], default="NHD")
+    parser.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=20)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    if (
+        args.query_tokens < 1024
+        or args.repeats < 1
+        or min(args.kv_tokens) < args.query_tokens
+    ):
+        parser.error("require query >= 1024, KV >= query, repeats >= 1")
+    import flashinfer
+
+    torch.manual_seed(2718)
+    page_size, heads, kv_heads, dim = 32, 16, 4, 256
+    query = torch.randn(
+        (args.query_tokens, heads, dim), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16
+    )
+    for length in args.kv_tokens:
+        pages = (length + page_size - 1) // page_size
+        cache = (
+            torch.randn((pages, 2, kv_heads, page_size, dim), device="cuda") * 6
+        ).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+        if args.layout == "NHD":
+            cache = cache.transpose(2, 3).contiguous()
+        indptr = torch.tensor([0, pages], dtype=torch.int32)
+        indices = torch.arange(pages, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+        plan = plan_expansion(
+            indptr,
+            indices,
+            num_query_tokens=args.query_tokens,
+            num_kv_heads=kv_heads,
+            page_size=page_size,
+            head_dim=dim,
+            budget=1 << 30,
+            layout=args.layout,
+        )
+        if plan is None:
+            raise RuntimeError("Requested geometry exceeds the expansion budget")
+        wrappers = []
+        for dtype in (torch.float8_e4m3fn, torch.bfloat16):
+            wrapper = flashinfer.BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper(
+                torch.empty(128 << 20, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda"),
+                args.layout,
+                backend="fa2",
+            )
+            wrapper.plan(
+                torch.tensor([0, args.query_tokens], dtype=torch.int32),
+                indptr,
+                indices,
+                torch.tensor([length % page_size or page_size], dtype=torch.int32),
+                heads,
+                kv_heads,
+                dim,
+                page_size,
+                causal=True,
+                q_data_type=torch.bfloat16,
+                kv_data_type=dtype,
+            )
+            wrappers.append(wrapper)
+
+        def native(wrapper=wrappers[0], cache=cache):
+            return wrapper.run(query, cache, q_scale=1.0, k_scale=0.125, v_scale=0.25)
+
+        def expanded(wrapper=wrappers[1], cache=cache, plan=plan):
+            gathered = expand_cache(cache[:, 0], cache[:, 1], plan)
+            return wrapper.run(
+                query, gathered, q_scale=1.0, k_scale=0.125, v_scale=0.25
+            )
+
+        reference, candidate = native().float(), expanded().float()
+        relative_difference = ((candidate - reference).norm() / reference.norm()).item()
+        print(
+            json.dumps(
+                {
+                    "query_tokens": args.query_tokens,
+                    "kv_tokens": length,
+                    "layout": args.layout,
+                    "repeats": args.repeats,
+                    "native": measure(native, args.repeats),
+                    "expansion_plus_attention": measure(expanded, args.repeats),
+                    "scratch_capacity_bytes": plan.cache.untyped_storage().nbytes(),
+                    "relative_difference": relative_difference,
+                }
+            )
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

 )
 ```
 
+### FlashInfer prefill cache expansion (SM120)
+
+`flashinfer_prefill_cache_expansion_bytes` is an opt-in optimization for
+long-prompt workloads where native FlashInfer attention is a prefill
+bottleneck. It aims to lower prefill latency and time to first token while
+retaining compact FP8 persistent KV storage and BF16 query precision. It
+defaults to `0` (disabled).
+
+Native attention with BF16 queries and FP8 KV converts cache tiles as it
+processes query tiles. Prefill with many query tokens can repeat that work
+for the same KV data. Expansion gathers referenced page entries into BF16
+scratch once per layer and prefill step, so attention can reuse the converted
+values. The tradeoff is an extra copy and temporary GPU memory. This is most
+promising when repeated conversions cost more than the copy; short prefills,
+mostly cached prompts and workloads limited by other operations may see
+little benefit. The decode path is unchanged.
+
+For example, allow up to 1 GiB of BF16 scratch per live attention metadata
+object on a supported configuration:
+
+```bash
+vllm serve <model> --dtype bfloat16 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
+  --attention-backend FLASHINFER \
+  --attention-config '{"flashinfer_prefill_cache_expansion_bytes":1073741824}'
+```
+
+The copy preserves finite E4M3 values exactly; attention still applies the
+original K/V scales. It introduces no additional quantization. BF16 attention
+can use different reductions, so output need not be bit-identical to the
+native FP8 path; check model quality as well as speed before adopting it.
+
+Expansion requires SM120, BF16 queries, E4M3 KV, head dimension 256, HND or NHD
+layout, causal native prefill, and at least 1024 query tokens summed across
+the prefill requests in the metadata batch. DCP, attention
+sinks, batch-invariant mode and full prefill/mixed CUDA graphs retain the
+native path. Unsupported configurations, batches exceeding the budget and
+scratch allocation failures also use native FP8 attention.
+
+The first eligible batch logs
+`Using bounded FP8 cache expansion for native prefill`. Later batches can
+still fall back if they exceed the budget or fail another eligibility check.
+
+The budget accepts 0 through 1073741824 bytes. Eligible metadata allocates a
+fixed-capacity buffer up to the configured budget even if fewer pages are used,
+reducing allocator churn. Concurrent metadata objects own separate buffers,
+so this is not a global memory cap.
+Larger budgets can accommodate more referenced pages, but consume memory
+that could otherwise support serving capacity. Compare prefill latency and
+time to first token against a zero-budget baseline, and check decode latency,
+throughput and concurrent serving capacity under mixed load. Enable it only
+when the measured benefit justifies the memory cost; no universal speedup is
+implied. Set the budget to `0` to disable it. A kernel comparison including
+the gather/cast is available in
+`benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_fp8_prefill_cache.py`; end-to-end serving
+measurements are still needed.
+
 ---
 
 ## Examples

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Page-selection, ownership and attention contracts for prefill expansion."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.v1.attention.ops.fp8_prefill_cache import (
+    PrefillCacheExpansion,
+    expand_cache,
+    expansion_bytes,
+    plan_expansion,
+    prefill_page_range,
+)
+
+
+def test_prefill_metadata_excludes_decode_pages():
+    indptr = torch.tensor([2, 5, 7], dtype=torch.int32)
+    start, end, compact = prefill_page_range(indptr, 9)
+    assert (start, end) == (2, 7)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(compact, torch.tensor([0, 3, 5], dtype=torch.int32))
+    torch.testing.assert_close(indptr, torch.tensor([2, 5, 7], dtype=torch.int32))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("offsets", [[-1, 2], [3, 2], [0, 10], [1, 5, 4]])
+def test_prefill_metadata_rejects_invalid_page_ranges(offsets):
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        prefill_page_range(torch.tensor(offsets, dtype=torch.int32), 9)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("layout", ["HND", "NHD"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("query_tokens,budget", [(1023, 1 << 30), (8192, 0)])
+def test_prefill_metadata_falls_back_before_cuda_allocation(
+    layout, query_tokens, budget
+):
+    assert (
+        plan_expansion(
+            torch.tensor([0, 2], dtype=torch.int32),
+            torch.tensor([1, 0], dtype=torch.int32),
+            num_query_tokens=query_tokens,
+            num_kv_heads=2,
+            page_size=32,
+            head_dim=256,
+            budget=budget,
+            layout=layout,
+        )
+        is None
+    )
+
+
+def test_prefill_metadata_budget_includes_keys_and_values():
+    geometry = dict(num_pages=3, num_kv_heads=2, page_size=32, head_dim=256)
+    required = 3 * 2 * 2 * 32 * 256 * 2
+    assert (
+        expansion_bytes(num_query_tokens=1024, budget=required, **geometry) == required
+    )
+    assert expansion_bytes(num_query_tokens=1024, budget=required - 1, **geometry) == 0
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not current_platform.is_cuda(), reason="CUDA kernel")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("layout", ["HND", "NHD"])
+def test_prefill_expansion_keeps_exact_values_and_independent_buffers(layout):
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(1729)
+    storage = (
+        torch.randn((12, 2, 32, 512), generator=generator, device="cuda") * 6
+    ).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    if layout == "NHD":
+        storage = storage.transpose(1, 2).contiguous()
+    keys, values = storage.split(256, dim=-1)
+    original = storage.view(torch.uint8).clone()
+    plans: list[PrefillCacheExpansion] = []
+    expected_first = None
+    budget = 1 << 20
+    for pages in [[7, 0, 7], [3, 8, 1, 3, 9]]:
+        raw_indices = torch.tensor(
+            [11, 0] + [item for page in pages for item in (page, 0)],
+            dtype=torch.int32,
+            device="cuda",
+        )
+        plan = plan_expansion(
+            torch.tensor([1, 1 + len(pages)], dtype=torch.int32),
+            raw_indices[::2],
+            num_query_tokens=1024,
+            num_kv_heads=2,
+            page_size=32,
+            head_dim=256,
+            budget=budget,
+            layout=layout,
+        )
+        assert plan is not None
+        assert plan.cache.untyped_storage().nbytes() == budget
+        expanded = expand_cache(keys, values, plan)
+        for index, page in enumerate(pages):
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                expanded[index, 0], keys[page].bfloat16(), rtol=0, atol=0
+            )
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                expanded[index, 1], values[page].bfloat16(), rtol=0, atol=0
+            )
+        if plans:
+            assert plan.cache.data_ptr() != plans[0].cache.data_ptr()
+            torch.testing.assert_close(plans[0].cache, expected_first, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        else:
+            expected_first = expanded.clone()
+        plans.append(plan)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(storage.view(torch.uint8), original, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not current_platform.is_cuda(), reason="FlashInfer requires CUDA")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("layout", ["HND", "NHD"])
+def test_prefill_expansion_preserves_scaled_ragged_attention(layout):
+    import flashinfer
+
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(1730)
+    storage = (
+        torch.randn((10, 2, 32, 512), generator=generator, device="cuda") * 6
+    ).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    if layout == "NHD":
+        storage = storage.transpose(1, 2).contiguous()
+    keys, values = storage.split(256, dim=-1)
+    indices = torch.tensor([8, 9, 4, 0, 4, 6], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    indptr = torch.tensor([2, 4, 6], dtype=torch.int32)
+    plan = plan_expansion(
+        indptr,
+        indices,
+        num_query_tokens=1024,
+        num_kv_heads=2,
+        page_size=32,
+        head_dim=256,
+        budget=1 << 20,
+        layout=layout,
+    )
+    assert plan is not None
+    expanded = expand_cache(keys, values, plan)
+    query_lengths, cache_lengths = [19, 11], [57, 43]
+    query = torch.randn(
+        (30, 4, 256), generator=generator, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16
+    )
+    results = []
+    for dtype, ptr, ids, cache in [
+        (storage.dtype, indptr, indices, (keys, values)),
+        (torch.bfloat16, plan.indptr, plan.indices, expanded),
+    ]:
+        wrapper = flashinfer.BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper(
+            torch.empty(32 << 20, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda"),
+            layout,

+        assert relative_error < 0.005

+    ).norm() / reference.norm()
+    assert relative_difference < 0.005

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Bounded, exact FP8-to-BF16 page expansion for native prefill.
+
+Materializing referenced page entries once per layer and prefill step trades
+scratch memory for fewer repeated conversions across attention query tiles.
+Calibration remains in the attention operation. This helper never applies
+scales and never mutates persistent KV storage. The caller must gate device,
+attention mode, query dtype and graph compatibility before planning.
+"""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+
+MAX_EXPANSION_BYTES = 1 << 30
+MIN_QUERY_TOKENS = 1024
+
+
+def prefill_page_range(
+    indptr: torch.Tensor, available: int
+) -> tuple[int, int, torch.Tensor]:
+    if indptr.device.type != "cpu" or indptr.ndim != 1 or indptr.numel() < 2:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "Prefill indptr must be a CPU vector with at least two entries"
+        )
+    if indptr.dtype not in (torch.int32, torch.int64):
+        raise ValueError("Page offsets must be integers")
+    start, end = int(indptr[0]), int(indptr[-1])
+    if start < 0 or end > available or bool(torch.any(indptr[1:] < indptr[:-1])):
+        raise ValueError("Invalid prefill page offsets")
+    rebased = indptr - start
+    if indptr.is_pinned():
+        rebased = rebased.pin_memory()
+    return start, end, rebased
+
+
+def expansion_bytes(
+    *,
+    num_query_tokens: int,
+    num_pages: int,
+    num_kv_heads: int,
+    page_size: int,
+    head_dim: int,
+    budget: int,
+) -> int:
+    if not 0 <= budget <= MAX_EXPANSION_BYTES:
+        raise ValueError("Expansion budget must be between zero and 1 GiB")
+    if min(num_pages, num_kv_heads, page_size, head_dim) < 0:
+        raise ValueError("Negative cache geometry")
+    size = num_pages * 2 * num_kv_heads * page_size * head_dim * 2
+    if num_query_tokens < MIN_QUERY_TOKENS or size > budget:
+        return 0
+    return size
+
+
+@dataclass
+class PrefillCacheExpansion:
+    source_indices: torch.Tensor
+    indptr: torch.Tensor
+    indices: torch.Tensor
+    cache: torch.Tensor
+    layout: str = "HND"
+
+
+def plan_expansion(
+    indptr: torch.Tensor,
+    page_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    *,
+    num_query_tokens: int,
+    num_kv_heads: int,
+    page_size: int,
+    head_dim: int,
+    budget: int,
+    layout: str = "HND",
+) -> PrefillCacheExpansion | None:
+    """Allocate a compact prefill cache, or retain native FP8 on budget/OOM.
+
+    ``indptr`` is the CPU prefill slice of the native paged offsets and may
+    start after decode entries. Each returned plan owns its scratch storage;
+    fixed capacity allows reuse by the allocator without aliasing live plans.
+    """
+    if layout not in ("HND", "NHD"):
+        raise ValueError("Only HND and NHD cache layouts are supported")
+    start, end, compact_indptr = prefill_page_range(indptr, page_indices.numel())
+    count = end - start
+    if not expansion_bytes(
+        num_query_tokens=num_query_tokens,
+        num_pages=count,
+        num_kv_heads=num_kv_heads,
+        page_size=page_size,
+        head_dim=head_dim,
+        budget=budget,
+    ):
+        return None
+    if page_indices.device.type != "cuda" or page_indices.ndim != 1:
+        raise ValueError("Page indices must be a CUDA vector")
+    if page_indices.dtype not in (torch.int32, torch.int64):
+        raise ValueError("Page indices must be integers")
+    if torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing():
+        return None
+    try:
+        # A stable capacity lets the allocator reuse buffers as context grows,
+        # instead of retaining a different allocation for each prefill chunk.
+        # Each metadata object still owns its buffer; live batches never alias.
+        capacity = budget // (2 * num_kv_heads * page_size * head_dim * 2)
+        shape = (
+            (capacity, 2, num_kv_heads, page_size, head_dim)
+            if layout == "HND"
+            else (capacity, 2, page_size, num_kv_heads, head_dim)
+        )
+        cache = torch.empty(shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=page_indices.device)[
+            :count
+        ]
+        compact_indices = torch.arange(
+            count, device=page_indices.device, dtype=page_indices.dtype
+        )
+    except torch.OutOfMemoryError:
+        # The caller has not planned attention yet and can use its FP8 path.
+        return None
+    return PrefillCacheExpansion(
+        page_indices[start:end], compact_indptr, compact_indices, cache, layout
+    )
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _expand_pages(
+    K,
+    V,
+    INDICES,
+    OUTPUT,
+    INDEX_STRIDE: tl.constexpr,
+    KP: tl.constexpr,
+    KH: tl.constexpr,
+    KT: tl.constexpr,
+    KD: tl.constexpr,
+    VP: tl.constexpr,
+    VH: tl.constexpr,
+    VT: tl.constexpr,
+    VD: tl.constexpr,
+    HEADS: tl.constexpr,
+    PAGE_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
+    DIM: tl.constexpr,
+    NHD: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    page = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+    physical = tl.load(INDICES + page * INDEX_STRIDE).to(tl.int64)
+    offsets = tl.program_id(1) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    mask = offsets < HEADS * PAGE_SIZE * DIM
+    head = offsets // (PAGE_SIZE * DIM)
+    token = (offsets // DIM) % PAGE_SIZE
+    dim = offsets % DIM
+    key = tl.load(K + physical * KP + head * KH + token * KT + dim * KD, mask, 0.0)
+    val = tl.load(V + physical * VP + head * VH + token * VT + dim * VD, mask, 0.0)
+    page_elements = HEADS * PAGE_SIZE * DIM
+    output_offset = token * HEADS * DIM + head * DIM + dim if NHD else offsets
+    destination = page * 2 * page_elements + output_offset
+    tl.store(OUTPUT + destination, key.to(tl.bfloat16), mask)
+    tl.store(OUTPUT + destination + page_elements, val.to(tl.bfloat16), mask)
+
+
+def expand_cache(
+    keys: torch.Tensor, values: torch.Tensor, plan: PrefillCacheExpansion
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Gather referenced pages exactly, preserving K/V calibration for attention.
+
+    K/V are strided ``[pages, heads, tokens, dim]`` or NHD views. The result
+    is ``[referenced_pages, 2, ...]`` in the same layout. Shared source pages
+    remain separate logical entries; persistent cache bytes are not modified.
+    """
+    if keys.ndim != 4 or values.shape != keys.shape:
+        raise ValueError("Expected four-dimensional K/V views with identical geometry")
+    if keys.dtype != torch.float8_e4m3fn or values.dtype != keys.dtype:
+        raise ValueError("Only E4M3 FP8 storage is qualified")
+    if keys.device != values.device or keys.device != plan.cache.device:
+        raise ValueError("Cache, indices and expansion must share a device")
+    if plan.cache.shape[2:] != keys.shape[1:]:
+        raise ValueError("Expansion geometry does not match the KV cache")
+    if plan.layout == "NHD":
+        keys = keys.transpose(1, 2)
+        values = values.transpose(1, 2)
+    if torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing():
+        raise RuntimeError("Prefill cache expansion is not qualified for full capture")
+    heads, page_size, dim = keys.shape[1:]
+    _expand_pages[(plan.cache.shape[0], triton.cdiv(heads * page_size * dim, 2048))](
+        keys,
+        values,
+        plan.source_indices,
+        plan.cache,
+        plan.source_indices.stride(0),
+        *keys.stride(),
+        *values.stride(),
+        heads,
+        page_size,
+        dim,
+        plan.layout == "NHD",
+        2048,
+        num_warps=4,
+    )
+    return plan.cache
